items.title: Jerry Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe and Christian Goodwillie, via Zoom, June 30, 2021
items.q: The transcript mentions Ornette Coleman only in the context of the venue name 'Gino’s Empty Foxhole' being named after the Ornette Coleman album title 'The Empty Foxhole'. There is no mention of a personal interaction, meeting, or professional relationship between Jerry Gordon and Ornette Coleman.

ctx.x: You had said in an earlier interview that Sun Ra was always pushing forward, his whole thing was to turn on the light upstairs with as many people as he could come in contact with. So I’m wondering if he turned on any lights for you? Either at this time or later with Evidence?

He turned lights on before I ever met him. When I was in college I had taken a trip to a college in another city to — and I met someone who played for me the album by Sun Ra “Nothing Is.” Okay? And that was my first exposure to Sun Ra, in a dorm room with someone playing the album “Nothing Is.” And it blew my mind. The first listen it blew © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-

my mind. The poetry on the cover, the poetry on the back cover, I mean that — I can’t say it resonated with me I would have to say it blew my mind, the music and the whole presentation. And then it just so happens that when I returned to Philadelphia, you know Sun Ra was living there and I would have opportunities to see him. Crazy.
